layers.note: A dwarf evergreen heath that carpets subalpine heather meadows, with white mountain-heather and Cascade blueberry.

moisture.note: Moist, acid, well-drained ground under a lasting snowpack.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; most on cool slopes where snow lies long.

elevation_m.note: Low in Alaska; subalpine and alpine, about 1,300 m and up, in the Washington Cascades.

shade_tolerance.note: Full sun to light shade at clump edges.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −15 to 1 °C; gone below −25 °C and above 5 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −38 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −45 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 6 to 15 °C; gone below 4 °C, where summers are too short, and above 18 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 500 to 2,600 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: About 120 to 1,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.6, gone by 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Pink mountain-heather grows from Alaska and Yukon south through British Columbia and the Cascades to the Sierra Nevada, and east to Alberta, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming (general range knowledge; not checked against PLANTS). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
